title: Tokenflow Congestion Odometer: End-to-End Probe for Continuous Batch Lifecycle under Mixed Arrival Profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible probe ("Tokenflow Congestion Odometer") that quantifies accumulated queue-dwell and batch-lifecycle friction under realistic mixed arrival patterns. Goal: expose how continuous batching + queueing interactions amplify tail latency (p95/p99) and lower effective tokens/sec across model variants and configs. This ticket describes the harness design, experiments to run, success criteria, and follow-ups for alerts and regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: Probe implemented and runnable as a containerized job that can target hosted/dedicated/private runtime endpoints with <60s startup
Produces a time-series metric 'queue_dwell_odometer' (ms*tokens) and per-session batch lifecycle traces exported to Grafana/Prometheus
Bench outputs include tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 token-latency, queue occupancy histogram, and per-token queue-dwell percentiles for each synthetic mix
Can detect a 10% relative increase in p95 latency with >90% statistical power over a 30-minute run (documented test)
Regression alert rule prototype implemented (EWMA + control-chart) and integrated into canary dashboard for manual review
tasks: Design synthetic arrival profiles: drip (low steady), cascade (short ramp bursts), stutter (microbursts), mixed-bimodal
Instrument runtime with queue_dwell and batch_lifecycle span tags (client and server side)
Implement client harness to play back arrival traces with tunable jitter, session affinity, and token-length distributions
Add exporter that aggregates per-window tokens/sec and p95, and computes queue_dwell_odometer
Run baseline experiments across three model variants (float32, int8-quant, 4-bit-quant) and two capacity configs (single-GPU, multi-GPU pool)
Analyze sensitivity to KV-cache warm/cold, prefix caching, and burst backpressure thresholds
Create dashboard panels and regression alert rules, document runbook
progress_updates: 2026-02-25: Kickoff meeting with Runtimes and Observability teams. Agreed to reuse the 'arrival-replay' library and extend it for session-aware batching.
2026-03-01: Prototype client harness implemented (nodejs) with three arrival modes. Initial smoke runs against dev cluster show expected queue occupancy signals.
2026-03-04: Added server-side tracing hooks to emit 'batch_open' and 'batch_close' events. Observability team suggested adding per-batch token_count tag — implemented.

2026-03-07: First full experiment: cascade + stutter mix against float32 model on single-GPU. Observed p95 amplification ~28% at scale factor 1.4; queue_dwell_odometer increased sharply during microbursts.
2026-03-09: Iterated on metric normalization: switched from raw ms*tokens to per-100k-token normalized odometer for cross-run comparability. Added EWMA baselining for regression detection.
2026-03-10: Dashboard draft ready in Grafana (shared link below). Draft regression rule using 30-minute EWMA windows under review by SREs.
decisions: Use a composite metric 'queue_dwell_odometer' (sum over tokens of queue_dwell_ms) because single percentiles miss accumulated cost across long-running sessions.
Favor 30-minute canonical runs for regression detection to balance statistical power vs. experiment duration for CI gating.
Normalize odometer to 'per-100k tokens' for cross-model comparisons and release notes.
Adopt EWMA + Shewhart-style control limits for alerting prototype; keep Mann-Whitney U testing in analysis scripts for post-hoc validation.
risks: Synthetic mixes may underrepresent real customer session correlations (e.g., correlated multi-route bursts). Mitigation: sample production traces for validation.
Instrumentation overhead could perturb tight latency SLOs on small dev pools. Mitigation: use lightweight tagging and sampling at 10% for production-like runs.
False positives in regression alerts during cluster maintenance or autoscaling events. Mitigation: annotate runs with infra events and exclude windows where scale events occur.
Quantization variants may alter per-token compute variance; comparing tokens/sec across quantized vs. float requires careful normalization.
test_plan: Smoke: 10-minute runs for each profile to validate telemetry and no runtime errors
Functional: 30-minute canonical runs for each model/config/mix; compute summary stats and odometer
Sensitivity: sweep arrival intensity (0.5x to 2.0x nominal) and burst shape parameters to map p95 amplification surface
Regression detection validation: inject controlled latency bump (+15% p95) and verify EWMA detects it within 1 window
Reproducibility: run selected experiments three times across different hours to quantify environmental noise
